core_obligations: Reduce to R epsilon_*(epsilon^*M) = M for M in QC(O) (proof lines 11633-11637): since R epsilon_* is fully faithful and epsilon^* composed with R epsilon_* is the identity, it suffices to show the other round trip is the identity on quasi-coherent objects.

Choose a K-flat representative and compute (proof lines 11638-11650): take a K-flat complex M^bullet of O-modules with flat terms representing M, so that epsilon^*M is represented by the tau-sheafification (M^bullet)^#; for U in C, Leray and the commutation of sheafification with restriction give R Gamma(U, R epsilon_*(epsilon^*M)) = R Gamma((C/U)_tau, (M^bullet|_{C/U})^#).

Compare with the tensor-up complex (proof lines 11651-11668): the map M^bullet(U) tensor_{O(U)} O_U -> M^bullet|_{C/U} has K-flat source by the pullback lemma, and because M is quasi-coherent this map is a quasi-isomorphism; since sheafification is exact the same holds after sheafification.

Conclude with assumption (2) (proof lines 11669-11675): hence R Gamma(U, R epsilon_*(epsilon^*M)) = R Gamma((C/U)_tau, (M^bullet tensor_{O(U)} O_U)^#), which assumption (2) identifies with R Gamma(U, M) = M^bullet(U), so the round trip is the identity as required.
proof_roadmap: Use fullness of R epsilon_* and epsilon^* R epsilon_* = id to reduce to showing R epsilon_*(epsilon^*M) = M on QC(O).
Take a K-flat representative of M and compute the right-hand side over an object U by Leray and the restriction compatibility of sheafification.
Identify the result with the expression in assumption (2) using quasi-coherence of M, and apply that assumption.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion — the cartesianity condition (2) against a chaotic topology — for epsilon^* and R epsilon_* to be mutually quasi-inverse equivalences between QC(O) and the full subcategory of objects whose pushforward is quasi-coherent (statement lines 11607-11630). The proof (proof lines 11632-11675) reduces by fullness to the single identity R epsilon_*(epsilon^*M) = M on quasi-coherent objects, chooses a K-flat representative, computes via Leray and the restriction compatibility of sheafification, and identifies the outcome with the expression controlled by condition (2). H2: one reduction and one explicit computation, both written out.
